# A full-screen program killed outright (kill -9 vim, kill -9 htop) or
# crashing never turns off what it turned on: mouse reporting, focus
# reporting, bracketed paste, the kitty keyboard protocol. The shell is left
# with them on, and escape bytes land in its prompt as the mouse moves or a
# key is pressed. The command's end (OSC 133;D) puts back the modes the
# shell had before it, so what the shell sets for itself stands.
# (`sh -c '…; kill -9 $$'` is a program that dies without tidying up.)
#
# Mouse and focus reporting are no shell's business, so they must be off
# whichever shell this is. `@SHELL@` is what tests/run.sh asks about the
# modes a shell does set for itself, which the restore must leave it: zsh
# and bash bracketed paste, fish 4 that and the kitty keyboard protocol.
type:sh -c 'printf "\033[?1002h\033[?1006h\033[?1004h\033[?2004h\033[>1u"; kill -9 $$'
key:enter
wait:1.2
expect-input-modes:mouse=off,focus=off@SHELL@
# Focus reporting off means no CSI I reaches the shell when the window takes
# the keyboard back: what's typed next is the command, nothing else.
focus-event:out
focus-event:in
type:echo DONE-$((40+2))
key:enter
expect:DONE-42
expect-not:command not found
# Nor does the mouse: a click with reporting left on would send its bytes to
# the shell as if they had been typed, and the next command would be the
# escape and the command run together.
click-text:DONE-42
type:echo TWO-$((1+1))
key:enter
expect:TWO-2
expect-not:command not found
